title: Magnets
description: Magnets attract ferromagnetic materials. Magnetic force can attract or repel. Stronger magnets have greater magnetic force. Magnets can solve engineering problems.

exercises.question: Which poles of two magnets ATTRACT each other?
exercises.exp: Opposite poles attract — North and South pull toward each other!

exercises.question: Which poles of two magnets REPEL each other?
exercises.exp: Like poles (N–N or S–S) repel — they push each other away.

exercises.question: Magnet A holds 20 paper clips. Magnet B holds 8. Which magnet is STRONGER?
exercises.exp: Magnet A can hold more paper clips, so its magnetic force is stronger!

exercises.question: Which material is attracted to a magnet?
exercises.exp: Iron (and steel) are ferromagnetic — they are attracted to magnets. Copper and aluminium are not.

exercises.question: As you move a magnet CLOSER to an iron nail, the magnetic force ___.
exercises.exp: Magnetic force increases as distance decreases — the closer the magnet, the stronger the pull!

exercises.question: A magnet can attract a paper clip THROUGH a thin book. What does this tell us?
choices: magnetic force passes through non-magnetic materials
the book is made of iron
exercises.exp: Magnetic fields pass through non-magnetic materials like paper, plastic, and water!

exercises.question: You use a magnet to separate iron filings from a sand mixture. This is an example of ___.
choices: using magnetic force to solve a problem
exercises.exp: Engineering use of magnets! Magnetic force separates iron (attracted) from sand (not attracted).

exercises.question: A compass needle always points NORTH because ___.
choices: all needles are made to point north
Earth has a magnetic field — the compass needle aligns with it
exercises.exp: Earth acts like a giant magnet with magnetic poles. A compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field!

exercises.question: Compare: A magnet attracts 5 paper clips from 1 cm away and 2 clips from 5 cm away. What can you conclude?
choices: distance has no effect on magnetic force
magnetic force decreases as distance increases
magnetic force increases as distance increases
exercises.exp: Magnetic force is strongest up close and weakens with distance — the data shows 5 clips (close) vs 2 clips (far).

exercises.question: An engineer uses a magnet to keep a cabinet door CLOSED. The magnet attracts a metal strip on the door frame. What poles face each other?
choices: it does not matter for this use
exercises.exp: Opposite poles attract — the magnet and metal strip face N–S, pulling the door shut!

exercises.question: What happens if you break a bar magnet in half?
choices: one piece has N only and the other has S only
both pieces become complete magnets with N and S poles
one piece is stronger than the other
exercises.exp: Every piece of a magnet is a complete magnet! Each half still has both N and S poles — amazing!

exercises.question: Which statement about magnetic force is TRUE?
choices: magnetic force only works by direct contact
magnetic force can act at a distance without touching
only large magnets have significant force
magnetic force and gravity are the same
exercises.exp: Magnetic force is a non-contact force — it acts across space without needing to touch the attracted object!

exercises.question: What are FERROMAGNETIC materials?
choices: materials strongly attracted to magnets (iron, nickel, cobalt, and their alloys)
exercises.exp: Ferromagnetic materials have a special atomic structure that aligns with magnetic fields — iron, nickel, cobalt, and steel are the main ones.

exercises.question: An engineer designs a MAGLEV (magnetic levitation) train. The train floats above the track using ___.
choices: like poles repelling — the train and track have same poles facing
opposite poles attracting the train upward
exercises.exp: Maglev trains use repulsion between like poles — the track and train both have N (or S) poles facing, pushing the train upward so it floats!

exercises.question: STEEL becomes magnetic when stroked by a magnet. Why?
choices: steel creates new magnetic poles from nothing
stroking aligns the tiny magnetic domains in the steel in the same direction
steel absorbs the magnetism from the original magnet
stroking heats the steel, making it magnetic
exercises.exp: Steel has tiny regions (domains) with random magnetic orientations. Stroking aligns these domains — making the steel act like a magnet!

exercises.question: If you HEAT a magnet to a very high temperature, it loses its magnetism. Why?
choices: heat removes the magnetic poles physically
heat energy causes the magnetic domains to become randomly oriented again
exercises.exp: The Curie temperature — above a critical temperature, thermal energy scrambles the domain alignment, destroying the magnet's organised structure.

exercises.question: MAGNETIC FIELD LINES flow from the ___ pole to the ___ pole outside the magnet.
exercises.exp: By convention, field lines exit the North pole and curve around to enter the South pole — like invisible arcs connecting the poles.

exercises.question: Which design would create the STRONGEST magnet?
choices: wrapping many coils of wire around an iron core and passing a large electric current through (electromagnet)
placing two weak magnets side by side
exercises.exp: Electromagnets with many coils of wire and a soft iron core can create enormously powerful magnetic fields — much stronger than permanent magnets!

exercises.question: An ELECTROMAGNET is turned ON and OFF by ___.
choices: turning the electric current on or off
exercises.exp: Electromagnets only work when current flows. Switch it on = magnet. Switch it off = no magnet. This makes them extremely useful in machines!

exercises.question: A junkyard CRANE uses an electromagnet to pick up scrap cars. When the crane needs to DROP the car, the operator ___.
choices: turns off the electric current — the electromagnet stops working
pushes the car with a pole
exercises.exp: Cut the current = cut the magnetism = the car drops! This controllable on/off ability makes electromagnets perfect for scrapyard cranes.

exercises.question: MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) machines in hospitals use extremely powerful magnets. What do they do?
choices: use powerful magnetic fields and radio waves to create detailed images of the inside of the human body
use heat to see inside the body
use sound waves like ultrasound only
exercises.exp: MRI machines use superconducting electromagnets (much more powerful than permanent magnets) to align hydrogen atoms and create detailed body scans — no radiation!

exercises.question: Why does a magnet attract an iron nail but NOT a copper coin?
choices: iron is a ferromagnetic material (attracted to magnets); copper is not magnetic
the magnet is too small for copper
exercises.exp: Only ferromagnetic materials (iron, nickel, cobalt, steel) are attracted to magnets. Copper, gold, aluminium are non-magnetic!

exercises.question: A bar magnet is placed on a table. Iron filings are scattered around it. What shape do the filings form?
choices: loops curving from one pole to the other — showing the magnetic field lines
a circle around the middle of the magnet
exercises.exp: Iron filings align along invisible magnetic field lines — they reveal the field's shape: arcing from North to South around the outside of the magnet.

exercises.question: The NORTH pole of Earth's magnetic field is actually near the GEOGRAPHIC south pole. Why does a compass point 'North'?
choices: the compass needle's North pole is attracted to Earth's magnetic South pole (near geographic North) — opposites attract!
exercises.exp: Earth's geographic North is near its magnetic SOUTH pole. The compass needle's N pole is attracted to it — so the compass points geographic North. Confusing but correct!

exercises.question: Two bar magnets are placed with N facing N. What happens?
exercises.exp: Like poles repel — N facing N creates a repulsive force pushing the magnets apart. Flip one and they attract!

exercises.question: Scientists use magnetic force to SEPARATE materials in recycling. What can they separate?
choices: iron and steel (magnetic) from aluminium and other non-magnetic metals
exercises.exp: Recycling plants use magnets on conveyor belts to pull out iron and steel — non-magnetic metals (aluminium, copper) pass through, allowing automated sorting!

exercises.question: A PERMANENT MAGNET keeps its magnetism without electricity. Where is it useful compared to an electromagnet?
choices: where you need to turn the magnetism on and off
where you need constant magnetism without a power source — fridge magnets, compasses, speakers
where you need extremely powerful magnetism
where you need to lift very heavy objects
exercises.exp: Permanent magnets need no electricity — perfect for compasses, fridge magnets, headphone speakers, and other everyday applications.

exercises.question: MAGNETIC NORTH changes slightly over time. Why?
choices: the North Pole moves south every year
Earth's liquid outer core flows, slowly shifting the magnetic field over decades
the sun moves the magnetic poles
exercises.exp: Earth's magnetic field is generated by flowing liquid iron in the outer core. As the flow slowly changes, so does the position of the magnetic poles!

exercises.question: A SPEAKER in a music system uses magnets to produce sound. How?
choices: magnets vibrate air on their own
electrical signals in a coil create a changing magnetic force that vibrates a cone, pushing air to create sound waves
magnets spin fans that create sound
exercises.exp: Alternating current in a coil interacts with a permanent magnet — the coil moves back and forth rapidly, vibrating a cone that creates sound waves!

exercises.question: Can two magnets repel each other WITHOUT touching?
choices: no — they must touch to interact
yes — magnetic force acts at a distance, even in air or through non-magnetic materials
only if they are very large
exercises.exp: Magnetic force is a non-contact force — it acts through the magnetic field in the space around the magnet. No touching required!

exercises.question: An engineer is designing a DOOR LATCH that uses magnets. She wants the door to OPEN easily but STAY CLOSED when shut. Which arrangement works?
choices: like poles facing (repulsion keeps door shut)
opposite poles facing (attraction keeps door shut — released with enough pull)
very strong electromagnets that require 1000V to release
exercises.exp: Opposite poles attract — the door magnets pull toward the frame, keeping it shut. A gentle pull overcomes the attraction to open it. Simple and effective!

exercises.question: Magnetic field lines show the direction a N pole would MOVE. They travel from ___.
choices: S pole to N pole outside the magnet
N pole to S pole outside the magnet
exercises.exp: Magnetic field lines go from N→S outside the magnet, and S→N inside. They never cross and are closest together at the poles (strongest force)!

exercises.question: The MAGNETIC DOMAIN THEORY explains magnetism. In a magnetised material ___.
choices: tiny regions (domains) align in the same direction — their fields add together
all domains point in random directions
exercises.exp: In unmagnetised iron, domains point randomly. In a magnet, domains align — their fields reinforce each other, creating a strong overall magnetic field!

exercises.question: Heating a magnet to high temperatures DEMAGNETISES it. Why?
choices: thermal energy causes magnetic domains to become randomly oriented again — they lose alignment
exercises.exp: High thermal energy causes domain vibration → random misalignment → overall magnetic field cancels out. Hammering a magnet also demagnetises it!

exercises.question: An ELECTROMAGNET uses electric current to create magnetism. When the current is switched OFF, the magnet ___.
choices: loses its magnetism immediately (for a soft iron core)
exercises.exp: Soft iron core electromagnets lose magnetism instantly when current stops — which is very useful for cranes that need to pick up then drop metal objects!

exercises.question: An electric GENERATOR works because ___.
choices: moving a wire through a magnetic field (or rotating a magnet near a wire coil) induces an electric current
heat from burning fuel is converted directly to electricity
light shining on magnets creates current
exercises.exp: Electromagnetic induction: changing magnetic flux through a wire induces current. Generators rotate coils in magnetic fields — all power stations use this principle!

exercises.question: A MOTOR is essentially a generator in REVERSE. It converts ___.
exercises.exp: Electric motors use current in a magnetic field to produce rotation (mechanical energy). Generators rotate to produce current. Both use electromagnetic principles!

exercises.question: MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) machines use magnetic fields of ___.
choices: about the same strength as a fridge magnet
about 1–3 Tesla — 20,000–60,000 times stronger than Earth's magnetic field
very weak fields similar to a compass needle
exercises.exp: MRI machines use superconducting magnets producing 1.5–3 Tesla — enormously powerful! This aligns hydrogen atoms in the body to create detailed medical images.

exercises.question: The AURORA BOREALIS (Northern Lights) is caused by ___.
choices: charged particles from the sun interacting with Earth's magnetic field and atmosphere, producing light
very cold temperatures in the atmosphere
volcanic gases in the upper atmosphere
exercises.exp: Solar wind particles are guided by Earth's magnetic field to the poles — where they collide with atmospheric gases, producing spectacular light shows!

exercises.question: HARD MAGNETIC materials (like rare-earth magnets) are preferred for permanent magnets because ___.
choices: they retain magnetism strongly and are difficult to demagnetise
they are softer and more flexible
exercises.exp: Hard magnetic materials (neodymium, alnico) have strongly aligned domains that resist randomisation. They make the most powerful permanent magnets!

exercises.question: In a MAGNETIC LEVITATION train, the train floats because ___.
choices: the train is lighter than air
powerful electromagnets beneath the train and in the track repel each other, lifting the train
exercises.exp: Maglev trains use repulsive magnetic forces to levitate — no wheels, no friction on the track. They can travel at over 600 km/h with very low energy loss!

exercises.question: Why can a PERMANENT MAGNET lose its magnetism over time if NOT stored carefully?
choices: physical shocks, heat, or nearby opposing magnetic fields can gradually randomise the magnetic domains
magnets naturally lose energy to the environment
magnets oxidise and rust, losing their magnetism
exercises.exp: Physical shocks and heat disrupt domain alignment — gradually demagnetising the material. Proper storage (with keeper bars) maintains domain alignment!

exercises.question: SUPERCONDUCTORS carry electrical current with ZERO resistance. They become superconducting ___.
choices: at room temperature when placed in a magnetic field
at very low temperatures (near absolute zero)
exercises.exp: Most superconductors work near absolute zero (−269°C). They also expel magnetic fields (Meissner effect) — this causes magnetic levitation in demos!

exercises.question: The COMPASS was invented in China about 1000 years ago. It transformed navigation because ___.
choices: it allowed sailors to determine direction without being able to see the sun or stars
exercises.exp: The compass enabled navigation in cloudy weather and at night — revolutionising maritime exploration. Chinese navigators used it centuries before Europeans!

exercises.question: Earth's magnetic NORTH pole is actually located near ___.
choices: northern Canada and Siberia — and it moves slowly over time
exercises.exp: Earth's magnetic north pole is currently in the Arctic but offset from the geographic pole and drifting about 50 km/year! Compasses show magnetic north, not true north.

exercises.question: A SEARCH AND RESCUE team uses a metal detector. The detector works by ___.
choices: measuring magnetic field changes caused by buried metal objects
exercises.exp: Metal detectors create electromagnetic fields. Nearby metal disturbs the field — the detector senses this change and alerts the user. Very effective for finding buried metal!

exercises.question: MAGENTIC STRIPE CARDS (old credit cards) store information by ___.
choices: magnetising tiny magnetic domains in the stripe to encode data in binary patterns
exercises.exp: Magnetic stripes contain millions of tiny magnetic regions — aligned N or S to represent binary data. Card readers detect this pattern to access your account!

exercises.question: Which quantity does a TESLA (T) measure?
exercises.exp: The Tesla is the SI unit of magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density). Earth's field ≈ 0.00005 T. MRI machines use 1.5–3 T. Named after Nikola Tesla!

exercises.question: MAGNETIC DECLINATION is the difference between ___.
choices: the strength of two different magnets
magnetic north (shown by compass) and true geographic north (shown on maps)
the north and south poles of a magnet
the top and bottom of a compass needle
exercises.exp: Magnetic declination varies by location and changes over time. Navigators must correct for it to use compass bearings accurately with geographic maps!

exercises.question: If you magnetise a piece of iron using INDUCTION (stroking with a magnet), the induced magnet's closest pole to the stroking magnet's north pole will be ___.
choices: south — opposite poles are induced at the point of closest contact
exercises.exp: Induction by contact: the iron end closest to the magnet's north pole becomes south (opposite poles align). Stroking in one direction aligns domains progressively.
